newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK PRIORITY IS 96 BUDGET DEF OF 7.6 PCT - ADVISOR.
newsitem.headline: GREEK PRIORITY IS 96 BUDGET DEF OF 7.6 PCT - ADVISOR.

text.p: The new Greek government's economic priority is cutting the 1996 budget deficit to 7.6 percent of GDP from 9.2 percent in 1995, the chairman of the council of economic advisors at the national economy ministry, Yannis Stournaras, said.
"The absolute priority of the economic team is to limit the 1996 general government budget deficit to 7.6 percent of GDP," Stournaras told Reuters.
"The target will be attained at any cost, mainly by slashing public spending and controlling subsidies," he said.
The EU convergence target for Greece's budget deficit in 1996 is 7.6 percent of GDP. There are no official figures on the present level of the deficit.

Andreas Makrypidis, president of the union of tax officials, told reporters the 1996 budget deficit would diverge from target by about 400 billion drachmas due to slower than projected tax revenue growth and spending overruns.

GDP growth is projected by the government at 2.6 percent in 1996, higher than the 2.0 percent figure in the 1996 draft budget, which has helped to improve the deficit to GDP ratio. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
